data.title: Noel Tata to become Voltas Chairman Emeritus as Sunil D'Souza takes over from Nov 12
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Voltas is set to undergo a leadership transition with Sunil Alaric D'Souza taking over as Chairman from November 12, as Noel N. Tata retires upon attaining the age of 70 in line with the Tata Group Governance Guidelines, the company said in an exchange filing.

The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on November 6, approved Noel Tata's retirement from the office of Chairman and Director with effect from the close of business hours on November 11, 2026. He will subsequently assume the position of Chairman Emeritus from November 12.

Tata has been associated with Voltas since 2003. The company said his leadership, strategic guidance and contribution had played an important role in shaping its growth trajectory, strengthening its market position and creating sustainable value.

The Board also appointed Sunil Alaric D'Souza as the new Chairman with effect from November 12. D'Souza is an existing Director on the company's board.

The company has also outlined a separate leadership transition at the managing director level, with Mukundan Menon C.P. scheduled to complete his tenure on May 24, 2027, and retire from the company's services on the same date, in accordance with the Tata Group's retirement policy for Executive Directors.

As part of the succession process, the Board has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head of the Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director for five years beginning May 25, 2027, subject to shareholder approval.

Balan has been redesignated as Head - Room Air Conditioner Business and Managing Director Designate until his appointment takes effect. He joined the Tata Group in 1999 through the Tata Administrative Service and moved to Voltas in 2001. He has held leadership positions across manufacturing, supply chain, strategy, international operations and consumer durables.

The Board has also approved the appointment of Venkatesalu Palaniswamy, Managing Director of Trent Limited, as an Additional Non-Independent Non-Executive Director of Voltas with effect from November 12, 2026.

The appointments and retirements form part of a broader leadership transition across the company's board and executive management.

Noel Tata's retirement from Voltas follows his scheduled exit from the boards of Trent and Titan, also upon attaining the age of 70 and in accordance with the Tata Group Governance Guidelines. Trent announced his retirement as Chairman and Director with effect from the close of business hours on November 11, 2026, appointing him Chairman Emeritus from November 12. Titan had separately announced that he would retire as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice-Chairman with effect from November 12.

data.title: Three warship manufacturing stocks to watch in India
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- India's rising defence spending and focus on modernising its armed forces have created significant opportunities for domestic warship manufacturers.

With the government pushing for self-reliance in defence production, a growing share of naval procurement is being directed towards Indian shipyards. Investments in advanced warships, submarines, frigates and aircraft carriers are expected to support the industry's long-term growth.

Here are three warship-manufacturing stocks to watch.

#1 Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders

Since 1774, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders has played a vital role in building India's maritime strength. It is India's only shipyard to have built destroyers, conventional submarines for the Indian Navy & manufactured corvettes in India.

MDL is the lead shipyard for building 4 Nilgiri-class stealth frigates. The company has also delivered the Kalvari Class submarines, with 6 submarines delivered between 2017 and 2025.

Overall, MDL has delivered 809 vessels since 1960, which also includes 34 warships, from advanced Destroyers to missile boats, and 8 submarines.

The company's performance in Q2FY27 was weak. Consolidated revenue dropped sharply to Rs.2,446 crore from Rs.2,929 crore, while net profit plunged 58% to Rs.346 crore from Rs.749 crore.

Meanwhile, MDL has signed an MoU with National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Andhra Pradesh to be the Anchor Shipyard for the proposed greenfield shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam, in Andhra Pradesh.

With an envisaged investment of Rs.150 bn and capacity of 1.2 m GT per annum, MDL will anchor the development of a globally competitive shipbuilding and marine ecosystem.

Cochin Shipyard Ltd (CSL) is among India's largest shipbuilding and ship repair companies. It gained prominence by constructing INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier.

The company also undertakes commercial shipbuilding, ship repairs and defence vessel construction. Its entry into more advanced naval platforms is an important development.

In September 2026, the company held steel-cutting and keel-laying ceremonies for Next Generation Missile Vessels (NGMV) for the Indian Navy. This provides an additional opportunity to participate in India's naval modernisation program.

Contract for construction of NGMVs was concluded with CSL in Mar 2023. The NGMVs are planned to be equipped with state-of-the-art weapon and sensors, which would significantly enhance the combat capabilities of the Indian Navy as a 'Future Ready and Combat Ready Force'.

Coming to the order book, the current unexecuted order book stands at around Rs.22,000 crore, which continues to provide CSL with good revenue visibility.

The company was also declared L1 for five next-generation survey vessels for the Indian Navy, valued at approximately Rs.50 bn. Once this contract concludes, the order book would be around Rs.270 bn.

Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd., is a Defence PSU, under the administrative control of ministry of defence, and a Navratna company.

GRSE has the distinction of becoming the first shipyard of independent India to build a warship for Indian Navy, the Seaward Defence Boat (SDB) INS Ajay, way back in 1961.

GRSE also built the first ever Indian Export Warship "CGS Barracuda" for Govt. of Mauritius, a Fast Patrol Vessel "SCG PS Zoroaster" for Seychelles and an Ocean-Going Cargo & Passenger Ferry Vessel "MV Ma Lisha" for Cooperative Republic of Guyana.

The company has built over 800 platforms, including 118 warships for Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard, and friendly foreign countries - highest number of warships built & delivered by any Indian shipyard till date.

In early November 2026, defence ministry signed contracts worth Rs.53,866 crore with Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) and Goa Shipyard Ltd (GSL) for the acquisition of eight Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for the Indian Navy. Under the contracts, GRSE will construct five corvettes, while GSL will construct the remaining three.

The project marks a milestone in India's indigenous warship design and construction capabilities, as it is the first project in which the ships will be indigenously designed by the Indian Navy and constructed by Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) selected through a competitive process.

The NGCs will be equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities - advanced missiles, weapons and sensor suites, enabling them to undertake missions across the air, surface and sub-surface domains.

In Q1FY27, the company recorded strong numbers. Revenue from operations increased from Rs.1,310 crore to Rs.1,815 crore, recording a growth of 39% YoY. Profit after tax rose 44% from Rs.120 crore to Rs.173 crore during the period.

lding

India's warship manufacturing sector is expected to grow due to the government's continued focus on defence modernisation and indigenous shipbuilding. The rising demand for advanced naval vessels provides long-term business opportunities for companies operating in this space.

However, investors should not overlook the risks. Defence projects often involve long execution timelines, cost overruns, and delays in order delivery. A strong order book does not automatically translate into immediate revenue or profits.

Further, valuations of some defence stocks may already factor in high growth expectations. Investors should therefore monitor quarterly performance, order execution and valuations rather than making decisions based on sector enthusiasm alone.

Investors should evaluate the company's fundamentals, corporate governance, and valuations of the stock as key factors when conducting due diligence before making investment decisions.

data.title: Bank holiday today: Are SBI, HDFC, ICICI branches open or closed on Saturday, 7 Nov ahead of Diwali? Check RBI calendar
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- There is no listed bank holiday today, on Saturday, 7 November, according to the central bank's official calendar. This means that all public and private sector lenders including the State Bank of India and HDFC Bank will be open for customers across India.

According to Reserve Bank of India's rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe listed holidays and mandatory closure on second and fourth Saturdays and every Sunday in a month. In-branch services are shut, but digital services (online net banking, app) will remain operational.

Since today, 7 November, is the first Saturday of the month and not a regional or cultural holiday, banks will remain open for customers across India.

Usually, in addition to the common national and gazetted holidays, or weekend offs, banks in India could have local holidays and festivals off, as required. The central bank releases its annual, official bank holiday list in January. Please contact your nearest local bank branch for their confirmed holiday schedule for 2026.

Banks will be closed for a total of 16 days this month, including state and regional holidays and weekend offs, as per the official RBI calendar for November.

Of this, banks, including the SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, PNB, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and other lenders across India will remain closed on the following date next week:

- November 8 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.

For customers who face urgent requirements or for daily spends, online banking services and bank mobile apps remain operational across the country even on official holidays and the weekends. You can thus use these uninterrupted services for convenient financial transactions.

- An individual can use UPI or the respective bank's app to make payments and receive money from others. These services work round the clock, whether banks are open or not. Though, at times, it may be down due to scheduled maintenance during which the banks will notify you.

- Additionally, fund transfer requests can be made using NEFT / RTGS transfer forms, demand draft request forms and cheque book forms.

- Apart from those options, credit cards, debit cards, and ATM cards can also be obtained through card services. Services such as account maintenance forms, setting up standing instructions, and applying for a locker are also available.

data.title: Best of the week | 'Don't fly,' said the court. India's travellers were already listening
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Best of the Week is a weekly newsletter by Siddharth Sharma/Shravani Sinha. Subscribe to Mint's newsletters to get them directly in your inbox.

"Don't travel by air," the Supreme Court said on Monday, declining an urgent hearing on a petition claiming airfares had jumped 700% before Diwali. The actual rise is smaller. But the bigger story may be this. Indians are flying less than they have in years.

Picture it this way. Imagine 100 passengers flew domestically in 2019. In May this year, 126.6 did. By July, that had crashed to 101.1, and September managed only 102.9. Not a dip. A slide. Those are levels worse than three years ago, wiping out the gains of 2023 to mid-2025. Traffic has fallen year-on-year in 10 of the past 15 months.

You might blame the West Asia war's disruption of international routes. But relative to pre-pandemic levels, domestic travel is now in worse shape than international, and has been since June. International traffic dipped in March and April, then bounced back. Domestic took longer to feel the pain, as costlier fuel was passed on to travellers with a lag, and it looks more lasting. Why the difference?

Fares are the obvious suspect. Retail airfare inflation crossed 20% in July and neared 30% by September, running four to six times the rise in overall travel costs. And that is before the festive season spike. In the pre-Diwali week, the cheapest one-way flights on popular metro routes cost 45-186% more than second AC rail tickets, against a usual premium of 25-30%.

Flying was never cheap in India. An average Indian needed 17 days of work to afford a ticket in 2023, higher than most emerging-market peers. Now even those who could afford it are feeling the squeeze. Icra points the same way. Elevated fares and weaker discretionary demand are keeping passengers at home.

Is this the start of a wider spending slowdown? Crisil's Jagannarayan Padmanabhan urges caution. Air travel is a useful signal, he says, but it is too early to call it conclusive evidence of a consumption downturn. A festive-season recovery is expected, though winning back lost ground will require a big jump. The industry itself expects the pressure to continue, with fuel costs and a weaker rupee still in play. Read the full story by Rupanjal Chauhan.

For years, an antibiotic sat at the top of India's pharma sales charts. Not anymore. Eli Lilly's Mounjaro has taken the crown, and the weight-loss drug boom is quietly rewriting a market built on cheap generics. Even generic semaglutide, at Rs.1,850 to Rs.8,000 a month, is flying off shelves, with volumes up nearly 16-fold in seven months. Patients, it seems, will now pay for more than a low price. But does a famous brand really work better? And with dozens of brands and devices crowding in, what will keep patients on treatment beyond the first few months?

Across India's biggest IT firms, employees are asking a question. What is the software meant to monitor their work activity actually measuring? ProHance chief executive Ankur Dhingra says the fear comes from poor communication. His preferred comparison is a Fitbit, and he insists users can switch off monitoring whenever they like. Reassuring, perhaps. Yet staff worry that automated metrics may misjudge smart work, and nobody is sure what else gets logged. Dhingra has a bigger headache, too. His clients have deep tech talent of their own. Could the very firms buying ProHance end up building it themselves?

Diwali is about to get its biggest blockbuster yet. Ramayana, a mega-budget epic with Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, opens Thursday in five languages, with IMAX shows nearly sold out. Trade experts expect a day-one haul of Rs.100 crore gross, and PVR Inox says record advance bookings have broken the pre-Diwali jinx. After years of lacklustre festive weekends, the stakes are huge for cinemas. A strong run could push 2026 past Rs.15,000 crore, the best year ever. But the movie reportedly cost Rs.4,000 crore to make. Will a great opening weekend be enough?

Donald Trump has taken an unprecedented blow, losing control of Congress in the mid-terms. Vice-president J.D. Vance blames the Iran war, and oil has already slipped below $100 a barrel on hopes of a settlement. For India, that could mean a lighter fuel bill, a calmer rupee and even a rethink on interest rates. Trade talks and tariffs could take a new turn too, while the AI sector faces a sentiment jolt. But a bruised Trump is an unpredictable one. Hours after accepting the results, he posted a picture that hints at what he may do next.

After last year's record rally, gold is up 15% this Samvat and silver nearly 20%. Yet both have slid sharply from January peaks, with silver down 51%. On Thursday, MCX Gold closed at Rs.1,43,184 per 10 grams and silver at Rs.1,87,490 per kg. As Muhurat trading opens Samvat 2083, analysts are split. Some are trimming gold. Others call this a buying window and say the worst is behind us. So which metal is for stability, and which for growth? And what approach do experts recommend to ride out the swings?

Nearly two-thirds of the 148 stocks recommended by brokerages for Diwali 2025 lost value over the following year, with almost a third falling more than 25%, a Mint analysis shows. Yet 53.4% still outperformed the Sensex, which declined 11.7% over the period. While a few picks delivered spectacular gains, others lost as much as 75%. The findings underline the risks of treating festive stock recommendations as investment cues. Experts say investors should look beyond benchmark outperformance and assess absolute returns, valuations, business fundamentals and risk.

The $6.3 billion Binance hack and a suspected data breach at the State Bank of India highlight the growing cybersecurity risks facing financial institutions. While hackers manipulated Binance's internal systems to steal digital assets, SBI found nearly 3,900 customer records containing personal information circulating on the dark web. No money was stolen from SBI, but the exposed data could enable phishing and identity theft. Experts point to weak credentials, insecure systems and third-party vulnerabilities as common entry points.

India's wealthy investors are exploring ways to gain exposure to Anthropic's upcoming IPO, which could raise $100 billion and value the AI company at up to $1.5 trillion. Wealth managers say technology founders, family offices and business executives are making repeated enquiries, but direct access is expected to be limited, with India excluded from the international offering. Scarce private-market shares and regulatory restrictions add to the hurdles. Advisers are instead suggesting listed proxies such as Amazon, Alphabet, TSMC and Samsung, which have links to Anthropic.

India's youthful population is set to age, with the share of people aged 60 and above projected to more than double over the next two decades. As fertility falls and the working-age population approaches its peak, the country will need to rethink policies around three groups: children, workers and the elderly. The article argues for a three-pronged approach: moving from population control to supporting families who want children, building affordable caregiving and healthcare systems for seniors, and creating jobs and cities that help young people live and raise families.

India faces three competing policy priorities: keeping prices affordable while allowing market forces to operate, balancing the interests of savers and borrowers, and attracting foreign capital without weakening fiscal health. Holding fuel prices down protects households but risks distorting markets and delaying inflationary pressures. Higher interest rates could curb inflation and improve returns for savers, but would raise borrowing costs for the government and businesses. Meanwhile, tax cuts may attract foreign investors as capital flows weaken and the rupee falls, but could reduce government revenues when spending pressures are rising.

That's all from us this week. Subscribe to our newsletters and the website for what's in the news and beyond it. Write to us at newsletters@livemint.com.

data.title: Amazon Doubles Down on Melania Trump Content With New Prime Video Series After $75 Million Documentary: Touts ‘Never-Before-Told Stories’
data.description:
Amazon.com Inc.‘s Prime Video will stream "MELANIA, The Series," a two-part show on first lady Melania Trump, starting Nov. 20, after spending $75 million on a documentary about the on first lady that earned about $16 million.

Series Follows Melania’s Return To The White House

Prime Video released a trailer for the series on Friday. The company said it offers "never-before-told stories," including her first days after the 47th Presidential Inauguration.

According to the announcement, the first episode, "Family & Trust," follows her priorities before returning to the White House. The second, "Pride & Honor," focuses on putting "her mission in motion," Prime Video said.

Amazon’s $75 Million Documentary Opened to $7 Million

The series follows Amazon’s "Melania" documentary, which covered the 20 days before President Donald Trump’s inauguration. Melania Trump was an executive producer.

Amazon spent $75 million to acquire and market the film. The film opened at an estimated $7 million, beating forecasts of $2 million to $5 million.

Political Scrutiny Over Alleged Amazon-Trump Ties

After the film’s release, Rep. Hank Johnson (D-Ga.) and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said they would investigate whether it was a "pay-to-play scheme." They cited Amazon’s financial interests tied to the Trump administration, the Hill reported.

Amazon Executive Chair Jeff Bezos attended the inauguration and has had a closer relationship with the president in his second term. Bezos denied any role in the acquisition of the film, the report added.

"Amazon’s a big company and makes a lot of decisions. But no, this idea that somehow that is a way of buying influence, it’s just not. It’s just not correct," Bezos said in May.

data.title: Noel Tata to retire as Titan Vice-Chairman on November 12 under Tata Group age policy
data.description:
Noel N. Tata will retire as Director and Vice-Chairman of Titan Company Limited on November 12, 2026, upon attaining the age of 70 years, in accordance with the Tata Group Governance Guidelines, the company said in an exchange filing.

In an exchange disclosure dated November 5, Titan said Tata would retire from the office of Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice-Chairman with effect from November 12.

The retirement is in line with the Tata Group’s governance guidelines, which prescribe 70 years as the retirement age for Non-Executive, Non-Independent Directors.

  • Read also: Noel Tata retires from Trent, to step down from other key group companies on Nov 12
Noel Tata’s association with the Tata Group

Tata, who was appointed to Titan’s board in March 2022, has been associated with the Tata Group for over four decades and holds leadership positions across several group companies.

He currently serves as Chairman of Trent Limited, Voltas Limited and Tata Investment Corporation Limited, while also holding the position of Vice-Chairman at Tata Steel. He is also Chairman of Tata International Limited and serves as Chairman of Tata Trusts.

Will other Tata Group positions be affected?

The development raises questions about whether the age-based retirement provision will lead to changes in his board positions across other Tata Group companies.

However, Titan’s November 5 filing only announces his retirement from its own board and does not indicate any decision regarding his positions in other group companies.

As per publicly available company disclosures, Tata was listed as Vice-Chairman of Tata Steel and Chairman of Trent, Voltas and Tata Investment Corporation in the respective corporate records and board profiles reviewed for this report. No corresponding retirement announcement from these companies has been established through the filings reviewed.

The cessation from Titan’s board will take effect on November 12, the company said.

data.title: From farmers’ challenges to product solutions: How R&D can improve agricultural productivity
data.description:
Agricultural research and development (R&D) must start with farmers’ problems and deliver measurable benefits in the field. Nutrient deficiencies, recurring pests and inefficient water use affect crop productivity and farmers’ returns; addressing them requires understanding the root causes and developing practical solutions, not simply new technologies. As Indian agriculture faces changing weather patterns, rising cultivation costs and pressure on natural resources, the measure of R&D success must be how effectively it improves farmers’ outcomes.

Understand the farmer before you design the solution

The performance of a crop depends on several interlinked factors such as soil health, nutrient availability, water management and pest incidence. Identifying the root constraint is important before determining the appropriate intervention. Researchers can learn about these interactions through soil analysis, field observations and farmer feedback, and can come up with solutions that are appropriate for particular crops and local conditions. This is particularly important in India, where variations in climate, soil and farm size make uniform recommendations difficult to apply effectively.

Turning scientific research into practical solutions

The transition from research to application necessitates thorough testing. Laboratory findings must undergo validation through field trials conducted across various locations and seasons to ensure consistency, safety, and suitability under diverse conditions. Additionally, results that differ between trials are crucial, as they can highlight areas where a formulation, dosage, or application method may require refinement.

Field validation needs to be an ongoing process, not a final checkpoint. Farmers’ experiences may shed light on practical constraints that controlled experiments cannot. Better collaboration between research institutions and industry can help turn validated findings into solutions that can be manufactured, are accessible and are relevant to farming needs. This demand-driven approach was also emphasised at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research’s 97th Annual General Meeting in August 2026.

Putting technology where it counts

Advances in artificial intelligence, sensors, remote sensing and precision agriculture are creating new ways to monitor crops and manage resources. Their value lies in helping farmers make better decisions: applying nutrients where they are needed, detecting crop stress early and managing irrigation more efficiently.

The potential is demonstrated by the outcomes of precision-agriculture interventions in India. According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, interventions in Goa resulted in a 4.69% and 6.58% increase in rice and cowpea yields, respectively, and a 92.9% reduction in irrigation water consumption. Such results are specific to the interventions and conditions studied but demonstrate why technologies must be assessed through measured outcomes rather than novelty alone.

Measuring innovation through farmer outcomes

Yield is an important indicator, but it cannot capture the full value of an innovation. Input-use efficiency, cultivation costs, crop quality, resource consumption and net returns also determine whether a solution benefits farmers. Consistent performance across seasons, affordability and ease of application are equally important to wider adoption. These factors must inform research and product development from the beginning.

The road ahead

Agricultural R&D must bring farmers, scientists, industry and technology providers into closer partnership. Farmers’ challenges should shape research priorities, while field trials and adoption experience should guide improvements. This approach keeps product development grounded in farming needs rather than technology alone.

Success is not simply bringing more technologies to market. It delivers reliable, practical solutions that improve productivity, use resources efficiently and strengthen farmers’ returns. By combining scientific rigor with field experience, agricultural R&D can turn innovation into lasting value where it matters most: on the farm.

data.title: Dhanteras sales 2026: How much gold and silver did Indians buy this year
data.description:
Gold and silver purchases witnessed strong demand on Dhanteras on Friday, November 6, with jewellers reporting higher showroom footfalls and advance bookings as a recent correction in precious metal prices encouraged consumers to make festive purchases.

While sales value is estimated to have risen across the industry, buyers largely preferred lightweight jewellery, smaller coins and lower-carat designs, reflecting a shift towards more affordable purchases amid elevated gold prices.

Gold sales by value are estimated to have increased 15-20% year-on-year to around ₹60,000 crore, according to preliminary estimates by the All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC).

However, the quantity of gold sold is likely to remain broadly unchanged from last year, as prices continue to be higher than their year-ago levels.

"Total gold business across India on the occasion of Dhanteras is estimated to be approximately ₹60,000 crore," said Rajesh Rokde, Chairman, All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC), in comments to PTI.

The GJC expects silver sales to increase 30% in value and 10% in volume.

Avinash Gupta, Vice Chairman, GJC, said showroom footfalls were higher than last year, with advance bookings supporting demand, particularly in western and northern markets.

What drove Dhanteras jewellery sales?

The recent correction in gold prices was one of the factors supporting purchases.

In Delhi, 24-carat gold was priced at ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams, including taxes, on Friday, compared with ₹1.83 lakh per 10 grams on January 29. However, the price remained above the ₹1.32 lakh per 10 grams recorded on Dhanteras last year.

Silver was quoted at ₹1.92 lakh per kg, down from its January 29 peak of ₹4.04 lakh per kg, but higher than the ₹1.70 lakh per kg recorded on Dhanteras last year, according to PTI.

Ramesh Kalyanaraman, Executive Director, Kalyan Jewellers, said the easing of gold prices provided an added impetus to festive purchases. The company saw demand for lightweight jewellery, including pendants, bangles and chains, along with smaller gold and silver coins and silver artefacts.

He also pointed to demand from Tier II and Tier III cities, including Jaipur, Dehradun, Surat, Belgaum, Ara and Raipur, where the company was seeing increased traction, including among first-time jewellery buyers.

Saurabh Gadgil, Chairman and Managing Director, PNG Jewellers, said early industry indications pointed to 25-30% incremental growth over last year, supported by lower prices, advance bookings and the extended Diwali weekend.

He said demand was visible across wedding and temple jewellery, lightweight gold and diamond jewellery, as well as silver articles. Old-gold exchange was also supporting purchases, particularly in smaller cities.

Lightweight jewellery and smaller-ticket purchases gain preference

The preference for affordable purchases was reflected in the demand for lower-carat and lightweight jewellery.

Colin Shah, Managing Director, Kama Jewelry, said the company recorded a 10% increase in jewellery sales compared with last year. Lightweight studded jewellery witnessed stronger demand, with 18-carat jewellery accounting for around half of sales. Buyers also opted for 14-carat and 9-carat designs, depending on their spending capacity.

Shah said heavy jewellery witnessed selective sales and bookings ahead of the wedding season, while gold coins weighing between 1 and 5 grams also attracted steady interest.

At the industry level, consumers were also using old-gold exchanges to fund fresh purchases.

Kirit Bhansali, Chairman, Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC), said higher precious metal prices had made consumers more selective, but had not significantly affected their willingness to buy. Wedding demand and gold exchanges continued to support the market.

Diamond jewellery and investment products also see demand

Demand was not limited to traditional gold jewellery.

Eshwar Surana, Managing Director, Raj Diamonds, said the company recorded around 20% growth in demand during the festive season compared with last year, alongside higher showroom footfalls and advance bookings.

He said some consumers who traditionally purchased gold were also exploring natural diamond jewellery for festive purchases and celebrations. Lightweight designs and coloured gemstones paired with diamonds were among the preferences he highlighted.

Sachin Jain, India CEO, World Gold Council, said retail walk-ins were strong, with purchases spanning jewellery, coins, bars, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and digital gold.

Samit Guha, Managing Director, MMTC-PAMP, said buyers are opting for smaller gold coins and bars and spreading purchases across different price points rather than committing to large purchases at one time.

Separately, Suvankar Sen, CEO, Senco Gold, said the company had recorded more than 25% growth in sales value compared with last year, supported by higher footfalls and wedding-related purchases.

Balram Garg, Managing Director, PC Jewellers, reported a 30-35% increase in sales volumes and 45-50% growth in value.

The All India Jewellers and Goldsmith Federation, part of the Confederation of All India Traders, said gold and silver sales had crossed ₹66,000 crore nationwide over the preceding several days, with Delhi's bullion markets recording business of more than ₹10,000 crore.

data.title: China Forex Reserves Edged Up in October — WSJ
data.description:
China's foreign exchange reserves rose slightly in October, against the backdrop of a strong Chinese currency that recently climbed to a multiyear high against the dollar thanks to strong exports.

The country's hoard of foreign exchange rose by $4.9 billion to $3.405 trillion at the end of October, the People's Bank of China said Saturday. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal expected end-October foreign exchange reserves of $3.41 trillion.

Largely unfazed by weak domestic economic data, the yuan climbed to a four-year high against the greenback in recent weeks. To tame the rally, the People's Bank of China tweaked forex reserve rules on Tuesday, requiring Chinese financial institutions to lock up more foreign-currency deposits with the central bank.

By tightening onshore dollar liquidity, the measure should moderate rather than reverse the yuan's appreciation, given strong export demand, according to Moody's Ratings. "The effect on exports will be small but positive, mainly by easing margin pressure on lower-end exporters," the agency's analysts said in a note this week.

ING economist Lynn Song suggests that raising the forex reserve requirement ratio for financial institutions signals the PBOC is pushing back against the speed of the yuan's appreciation. He also notes the action is largely symbolic, stopping short of a sharp intervention like aggressively adjusting the currency's daily reference rate.

While Beijing has been greenlighting yuan's gradual rise, analysts say the PBOC's move this week is a clear sign that policymakers have no appetite for a fast currency appreciation that would dent Chinese exporters' global competitiveness.

Extending its buying streak to two full years, China's central bank boosted its gold holdings in October to 78.3 million troy ounces, up from 77.47 million the previous month, data released Saturday showed.

data.title: Petrol, diesel prices on 7 November: Check how much fuel costs in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata - Full list
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Petrol and diesel prices today, November 7: Petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged in most cities on Saturday after the Centre reduced the additional excise duty on petrol exports. The Finance Ministry recently notified a revised duty structure that took effect on October 31. Under the new structure, the export duty on petrol was reduced from Rs.2.50 per litre to zero.

While the export duty on petrol was scrapped, the levy on diesel was increased from Rs.8.50 per litre to Rs.11.50 per litre.

Fuel prices vary across major cities and states largely due to factors such as local taxes, including Value Added Tax (VAT), freight charges and other local considerations. Although geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have led to fluctuations in global oil prices, domestic retail fuel rates have largely remained unchanged, offering some relief to consumers.

*Source: Goodreturns

According to a Reuters report, India's oil consumption rose by around 10% in October to 20.49 million metric tonnes from 18.71 million tonnes in September, marking its highest level since March 2026. Data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the Oil Ministry showed that consumption was also 2.7% higher than in October last year.

Diesel consumption increased by 19% in October compared with the previous month and was up 12% year-on-year. Gasoline sales rose 3.5% from the corresponding month last year.

Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) consumption, meanwhile, declined by nearly 1% in October to 2.52 million metric tonnes compared with September. It was also down around 12.3% from a year earlier.

Overall, fuel consumption increased by 6.4% from September.

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) is increasing its crude oil purchases on a delivered basis to reduce its exposure to shipping risks arising from the Iran war and lower freight costs, its head of finance said on Wednesday.

Oil prices posted modest gains late Friday amid renewed concerns over a possible escalation of US military action against Iran. US President Donald Trump said he would soon decide whether to pursue a peace agreement with Tehran or launch further attacks to destroy what remains of the country.

Brent crude futures for January delivery settled at $98.32 per barrel, up 3 cents, or 0.03%. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures ended at $90.83 a barrel, gaining 31 cents, or 0.34%.

Despite Friday's marginal gains, Brent is on course for a weekly decline of around 17%. If sustained, this would mark its steepest weekly percentage fall since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and its biggest decline in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.

WTI is also heading for a weekly decline of around 13%.

data.title: ED searches 3 premises linked to CoinDCX, Delta Exchange in FEMA case
data.description:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Bengaluru, has conducted searches at three premises linked to cryptocurrency platforms CoinDCX and Delta Exchange over alleged unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving crypto derivatives and Real World Asset (RWA) tokens.

In a post on X on November 6, the agency said the searches were conducted under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999. The searches took place on November 4 and 5 at premises linked to Neblio Technologies Pvt. Ltd., which operates CoinDCX, and Excelium Technologies Pvt. Ltd., which operates Delta Exchange India.

According to the ED, both platforms offered spot trading in cryptocurrencies, futures and options in crypto tokens, and trading in tokenised stocks of foreign companies. The agency is examining whether these activities involved unauthorised cross-border transactions.

What has the ED alleged?

The ED's preliminary investigation indicated that customer funds deposited in Indian rupees on CoinDCX were converted into USDT, a stablecoin, and transferred to overseas cryptocurrency exchanges, including Binance, KuCoin and Gate.io, to execute trades.

The agency alleged that these transactions were routed through an account held in the name of a Costa Rica-based entity, which it described as a paper entity. It said the transactions were also executed through CoinDCX's application programming interfaces (APIs).

The agency said the volume of cross-border spot trading transactions ran into thousands of crores of rupees.

The ED also alleged that CoinDCX facilitated cryptocurrency futures and options trades by opening corresponding positions on overseas exchanges, including Binance, KuCoin, Bybit and Gate.io. According to the agency, these positions were linked to customer trades on the Indian platform, with settlements taking place on the overseas exchanges.

Delta Exchange transactions under investigation

The ED alleged that a large volume of futures and options trades and tokenised stock transactions offered by Delta Exchange India were routed through CoinDCX, which then executed corresponding transactions on overseas cryptocurrency exchanges.

The agency said these cross-border transactions involved several thousand crores of rupees. It is also investigating alleged transfers of hundreds of crores of rupees by Delta Exchange India to its overseas associate entities.

The ED is examining the regulatory compliance of products offered by both platforms under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the SEBI Act, 1992, and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, among other laws.

The agency said further investigation is underway.

data.title: India moves to set standards for hydrogen-powered trucks
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- The government is moving to standardize hydrogen-powered truck engines and testing procedures as India looks to develop alternatives to diesel for freight transport and cut emissions from heavy-duty vehicles.

The new and renewable energy ministry (MNRE) is working with the government-run auto testing agency, the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), to develop and standardize hydrogen-internal combustion engine (H2-ICE) powertrains, according to two people aware of the development and ARAI's annual report.

The development comes amid mounting concerns over vehicular pollution, particularly in cities such as Delhi, which experience severe air pollution during the winter months.

Decarbonising freight transport is also important because even if diesel trucks account for around 5% of India's vehicle fleet, they contribute more than a third of the transport sector's carbon emissions. This makes heavy-duty vehicles an important target for India's broader goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.

ARAI's work under this project involves developing direct-injection hydrogen engine for heavy trucks, and establishing testing protocols for H2-ICE and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles (H2FCV), noted the testing agency's fiscal year 2026 (FY26) annual report.

H2-ICE engines burn hydrogen to generate power, much like conventional diesel engines. Fuel-cell vehicles use hydrogen to generate electricity, which drives an electric motor.

"Along with developing H2FCV powertrains for buses, the MNRE's project with ARAI will also contribute towards transport sector targets under India's Green Hydrogen Mission," said the first person cited above, requesting anonymity.

The work to standardize hydrogen powertrains and their testing is part of the National Green Hydrogen Mission, a Rs.19,744-crore initiative approved in January 2023 to make India a global hub for green hydrogen production, use and exports. The transport sector is among the mission's targeted areas for hydrogen adoption.

Automakers such as Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland have hydrogen-based truck models, while the government has stepped up trials of hydrogen-powered buses and trucks. These include five hydrogen fuel-cell buses in Leh in 2023-24, fuel-cell bus trials in Delhi-NCR in 2023, and the pilot projects announced in March 2025 under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, covering 37 buses and trucks across 10 routes, according to official government statements.

Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari described hydrogen as "the fuel of the future" at an event in New Delhi on 4 November.

"Hydrogen vehicles are also a part of the government's long-term vision for India's auto sector," said the first person.

A February 2026 report by Niti Aayog on decarbonising India's vehicle emissions by 2070 said hydrogen powertrains could complement electric vehicles, especially in long-haul freight.

The government has also extended policy support to hydrogen fuel cell vehicles under the Rs.25,938-crore production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto parts, which allows eligible automakers to claim incentives till FY29.

India currently produces around 6.5 million tonnes of hydrogen annually, predominantly using fossil fuels, a process commonly referred to as grey hydrogen.

Research by the Indian government's principal scientific advisor (PSA) in 2023 showed that a heavy-duty hydrogen ICE truck had an efficiency of 8.1 km per kilogram of hydrogen in testing on the Delhi-Jaipur corridor. At an annual distance of 60,000-70,000 km, such a truck would require around 7.4-8.6 tonnes of hydrogen.

India's annual green hydrogen production capacity reached 8,000 tonnes per year as of February 2026, MNRE minister of state Shripad Yesso Naik informed the Rajya Sabha in March.

Scaling up green hydrogen production remains a challenge, with the availability and cost of electrolysers among the constraints. Electrolysers use electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.

"We are running many pilots in the transport sector for hydrogen usage," said a government official aware of the development, the second person cited above, requesting anonymity.

Queries emailed to MNRE, ARAI, and truck makers Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland on 26 October remained unanswered till press time.

Experts said hydrogen powertrain pilots in commercial vehicles have been running for the last few years, but standardizing the testing of hydrogen vehicles and making standards for H2-ICE and H2FCV powertrains could act as guardrails for the industry.

"Engine makers have started to make H2-ICE engines over the last few years, and the same goes with H2FCV powertrains. Both these are mostly deployed in pilot projects at the moment," said Sharif Qamar, associate director of transport and urban governance at New Delhi-based think tank The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI).

"This intervention of standardisation will give guardrails for the industry to approach hydrogen powertrains. This will set, in a way, the minimum requirements, the benchmarks, for H2-ICE and fuel cell vehicles," he said.Qamar, however, said that development of fuel infrastructure for hydrogen powertrains would be crucial to the proliferation of this zero-emission technology, especially along highway corridors to support freight movement.

ARAI receives funding from the ministry of heavy industries for specific initiatives, such as under the PM E-Drive scheme, which had an outlay of Rs.780 crore for four testing agencies, including ARAI.

The Pune-based testing agency also receives funds from the industry for commercial testing services.

data.title: Peltola campaign sues Alaska to get records on rejected absentee ballots
data.description:
Key points:
  • About 600 votes separate Peltola and Sullivan with ballots still being counted
  • Plaintiffs seek records identifying rejected absentee ballots
  • State says law does not require release; records treated as confidential

By Daniel Trotta

The campaign of Democratic US Senate candidate Mary Peltola of Alaska sued state election officials on Friday seeking the immediate release of records identifying absentee ballots that were rejected in Tuesday's voting.

Peltola and the Republican candidate, incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan remain locked in a close contest for the seat, with about 600 votes separating them as ballots from remote areas in the sprawling state were still being counted.

With such a narrow margin separating the candidates, the race could hinge on ballots that were mailed or that have to be flown in from remote communities. The state will accept ballots up to November 18.

Democrats captured control of the US Senate as part of their sweeping victory across the country in the midterm elections. The undecided Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi will determine whether the Democrats can expand on their 54-seat majority in the 100-member chamber.

Peltola's campaign group, Alaskans for Mary, sued the Alaska Division of Elections, Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom and Director of Elections Carol Beecher, seeking the release of records identifying absentee ballots rejected in Tuesday's election and the reasons for those rejections.

The campaign says it requested the records on October 27 and again on Wednesday under Alaska’s Public Records Act but received no response, and was later denied immediate access.

The plaintiffs also sought a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction to compel the immediate release of the records, arguing that time is critical because ballot counting and certification are under way.

Friday's filing argues that a lack of prompt access would leave Alaskans for Mary unable to monitor whether ballots are being properly counted and whether Peltola supporters had their ballots improperly rejected, as alleged in the lawsuit.

The state Department of Law, which represents the lieutenant governor and the Division of Elections, said in a statement that the Division of Elections has long treated those records as confidential and that Alaska law does not require their release.

"Because the information is preliminary, subject to change, and not yet available to affected voters, the Division does not distribute the records separately or allow observers to retain them," the statement said.

"Releasing preliminary information in the manner sought by the lawsuit would create additional burdens during ballot processing and could delay the timely counting of votes. The Division has protected this information for years and will ask the court to protect it too," the statement said.

Sullivan's campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: VanEck CEO Warns Next US Financial Crisis Will Start In Washington, Urges Investors To Hold ‘Real Assets’ Like Gold and Bitcoin
data.description:
Key points:
  • VanEck CEO Jan van Eck urged investors to hold gold and Bitcoin.
  • He said that these assets will act as a hedge against U.S. government spending, and remain a long-term Bitcoin bull.
  • Van Eck expects the U.S. to inflate its way out of its debt, and doesn't think AI will ease the pressure by pushing prices down.

VanEck Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jan van Eck said that the next U.S. financial crisis would begin in Washington rather than in the banking system, and said investors should hold "real assets" like gold and Bitcoin (BTC) as protection.

In an interview with Anthony Pompliano on Thursday, van Eck said, "For the entirety of U.S. history," financial crises have started with banks. This time, however, he expected the trouble to come from government debt. "This is going to be started in D.C. and no one can bail us out. And I think the rest of the world sees this," he said.

That outlook shaped his view on portfolios. When asked how investors could protect themselves from U.S. government spending, van Eck pointed to hard assets. "You have to have real assets, gold and Bitcoin in your portfolio. You don't know if it'll pay off," he said. He was clear about his position on Bitcoin over the longer run, and said, "I'm a long-term bull, so I definitely think it would be higher in 10 years.

No AI Bailout

Van Eck saw no easy way out for Washington, and said, "We're going to inflate our way out of our debt."

"There's no easy answer, and it's not going to be pretty." He also dismissed the idea that artificial intelligence (AI) would ease the pressure by pushing prices down. "All technology is deflationary," he said. "There was great technology in the 70s, but we had runaway inflation."

Bitcoin's price was down by 0.2% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin was in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it was at 'normal' levels over the past day.

Where Does Van Eck See Value?

Rather than adding more crypto products, VanEck is now pushing active management. He said it made sense because most financial advisers struggled to choose between tokens like Avalanche (AVAX) and Ethereum (ETH). "Most advisors can't pick Avalanche versus Ethereum or these kinds of things," he said.

According to the VanEck CEO, layer-1 blockchains, the base networks that other crypto applications run on, along with the trading platforms, would hold up. "The foundational ones will survive, I think, and then the exchanges, I think, will survive," he said.

For investors who want exposure beyond those two groups, van Eck's advice was to leave token picking to a fund. "Otherwise, go with an index or go with an active managed fund," he said.

AVAX's price was trading around $8, flat over the last 24 hours, while Ethereum's price was trading at $2,240, up over 0.2%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around AVAX and ETH both remained in the ‘bearish’ zone.

data.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation: Report
data.description:
OpenAI has closed on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with the matter said on Friday (November 6).

The $11 billion raised so far represents only a portion of OpenAI’s original target of up to $30 billion, while the company’s valuation has come down from the $1.5 trillion level it had initially sought, two investors said.

SoftBank and MGX participated in the funding, the investors said.

Bloomberg News reported on the funding earlier on Friday (November 6).

Sentiment toward AI companies has cooled in the last month, with some investors valuing rival Anthropic’s planned IPO at about $1.5 trillion, below earlier expectations of roughly $2 trillion.
